deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous page studies the quartic X(x) = x^4 - 2x^2 + 3x + 10. It finds the critical points (roots of X'(x)/4 = x^3 - x + 3/4) and the critical values (X = -x^2 + 9/4 x + 10 on those roots). It then tabulates, for r = 2.6, where the real and imaginary parts of X vanish on a circle. This page does the same for r = 2.2 and r = 2.0. The next page continues with r = 1.7 and Newton-corrects the root x ≈ 1.44988 + 1.27257i. This is a numerical tracing of the curves Re X = 0 and Im X = 0 in the plane x = r e^{iφ}: the curves whose intersections are the roots in Gauss's 1799 proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra.

Setup (my notation). With x = r e^{iφ}:
- Re X = r^4 cos4φ - 2r^2 cos2φ + 3r cosφ + 10
- Im X = r^4 sin4φ - 2r^2 sin2φ + 3r sinφ

(1) r = 2.2 (log r = 0.34242). The header logs are the coefficients:
- 0.81954 = log(3r) = log 6.6
- 0.98588n = log(-2r^2) = log(-9.68)
- 1.36969 = log(r^4) = log 23.4256

Each following row gives one angle φ and the logs of the three trig factors (φ, 2φ, 4φ), so that the three terms can be added.
- Rows using cosines are solutions of Re X = 0: φ = 29°18'13'', 55°39'8'', 119°54'17'', 159°40'4''.
- Rows using sines are solutions of Im X = 0: φ = 41°46'48'', 86°38'3'', 143°33'14''.
- Example (φ = 29°18'13''): log cos = 9.94054, log cos2φ = 9.71676, log cos4φ = 9.66022n. The terms are 5.755 - 5.042 - 10.713 = -10.000, so Re X = 0.
- Example (φ = 41°46'48''): the terms are 4.398 - 9.619 + 5.222 ≈ 0, so Im X = 0.

The zeros alternate Re, Im, Re, Im, … around the upper semicircle (Im X also vanishes at φ = 0 and 180°), as the 1799 proof requires for a large circle. The right-hand column gives the points r(cosφ + i sinφ), e.g. 1.9185 + 1.0768i. One line (155°58') was struck out and replaced by 159°40'4''.

(2) 'Correlate für 41°46'48''' (the other points of Im X = 0 on the same line through 0).
- Write x = t e^{iφ} with t real of either sign. Then Im X = t sinφ · (4cosφ cos2φ · t^3 - 4cosφ · t + 3) (my derivation).
- So for fixed φ the curve Im X = 0 meets the line in the three roots of a cubic in t with no t^2 term. The roots therefore sum to 0.
- With t1 = 2.2, Gauss gets log t2 = 0.07888 (t2 = 1.1992) and log t3 = 0.53135n (t3 = -3.3992).
- The points are 1.6406 + 1.4658i, 0.8942 + 0.7990i and -2.5348 - 2.2648i. Their sum is 0, as a check.

(3) r = 2.0 (log 2 = 0.30103). The divided-out coefficients are listed: 9.57403 = log(3/8), 9.69897n = log(-1/2), 0.00000 = log 1. So Re X/16 = cos4φ - ½cos2φ + ⅜cosφ + 5/8 and Im X/16 = sin4φ - ½sin2φ + ⅜sinφ.
- Re X = 0 at 34°51'1'', 49°37'33'', 122°23'22'', 158°51'½'' (written 158.31.29; see errors).
- Im X = 0 at 41°24'34'', 85°39'32'', 145°39'32''.
- The listed points are 2e^{iφ}.

(4) 'Correlate für 41.24.34', the exact case.
- Here cosφ = 3/4 and sinφ = √7/4. The cubic becomes (3/8)t^3 - 3t + 3 = 0, i.e. t^3 - 8t + 8 = 0.
- Its roots are t = 2 and t = -1 ± √5.
- The points are 3/2 + (√7/2)i; (√5-1)(3/4 + √7/4 i) = ¾√5 - ¾ + (¼√35 - ¼√7)i = 0.92705 + 0.81758i; and -(√5+1)(3/4 + √7/4 i) = -2.42705 - 2.1405i.
- At t = 2, X = -2 exactly (real).

Purpose: comparing r = 2.2, 2.0 and 1.7 shows the two Re X = 0 branches near φ ≈ 35° and 50° closing in on the Im X = 0 branch near φ ≈ 41.4°. This brackets the root of modulus about 1.929 at angle 41°16', which the next page computes and corrects to 1.44988084 + 1.27257144i.
errors: r = 2.0, last entry: the angle written 158.31.29 does not match the point -1.8654 + 0.7214i on the same line. That point has argument ≈ 158°51.5', and Re X = 0 there (the residual of Re X/16 is ≈ -1e-4). At 158°31'29'' the residual of Re X/16 is ≈ -0.018. So the minutes should be 51, not 31 (a slip by Gauss or a misreading); the complex value itself is correct.
r = 2.2, row 55°39'8'': cos(2φ) = cos 111.3° is negative, but the log 9.56029 carries no 'n'. The resulting value Re X ≈ 0 is nevertheless correct, so this is a sign-marking omission only.
Minor last-digit differences only: the second correlate has log 1.19917 = 0.07888-0.07889, and 2.2·cos(143°33'14'') = -1.7698. Otherwise all checked values agree to the stated places.

results.what: Numerical tracing, on circles |x| = 2.2 and 2.0, of the angles where Re X = 0 and Im X = 0 for X = x^4 - 2x^2 + 3x + 10, showing that they interlace and that the curves converge toward a complex root
results.modern_name: zero curves of the real and imaginary parts of a polynomial (the geometric argument of the fundamental theorem of algebra; argument principle / winding behaviour)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss, 1799 dissertation (curve-intersection proof of the FTA)

results.what: Along the ray x = t e^{iφ}, Im X = 0 reduces to the depressed cubic 4cosφcos2φ·t^3 - 4cosφ·t + 3 = 0, whose three roots sum to zero; this gives the three 'correlate' points of Im X = 0 on one line, exactly so for cosφ = 3/4 (t^3 - 8t + 8 = 0, t = 2, -1 ± √5)
results.modern_name: intersection of a line through the origin with the real-axis preimage curve Im p = 0
results.usually_credited_to: elementary; part of Gauss's own working of his FTA illustration

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine numerical computations illustrating the curve-intersection picture of Gauss's own 1799 FTA proof, possibly the working behind a figure for the example quartic x^4 - 2x^2 + 3x + 10. Nothing here is attributed to later authors.
